projects.title: Finora
projects.overview:
Finora is a business accounting application designed around the daily work of UAE trading and service companies. Sales, purchases, expenses and inventory connect to a double-entry ledger. Teams can review invoices, payments, bank transactions and reports within the same organisation workspace.

The implementation uses Next.js, TypeScript and Prisma, with money stored in integer minor units. The source includes balanced journal posting, reversing entries, document numbering, inventory movements, UAE VAT handling and role-based access. The device mockups were captured from a local build running demonstration data for a fictional trading company; no customer or financial records are shown.

Users move from a customer or supplier record to a commercial document, then to posting and settlement. Every invoice shows the journal entries it created, so staff can trace a balance back to its source. The dashboard summarises cash, receivables and payables and links overdue items to the underlying records.

Financial documents feed balanced journal entries rather than isolated dashboard totals. The code represents amounts in fils and handles corrections through reversing entries. Tenant context, roles and server-side validation are part of the implementation, alongside reporting, approvals and recurring documents.

Developed application; not deployed to a public live URL. The documented scope includes accounting, inventory, banking, reports and account administration. The assistant and external services depend on their configured providers. Tax settings and financial reports need business-specific review before operational use; the portfolio does not represent regulatory certification.

projects.title: Nexora
projects.overview:
Nexora is a help desk and work management application for teams handling service requests alongside everyday tasks. Staff can assign tickets, track status, add internal notes and coordinate project work. Customers have a separate portal, while organisation-level permissions keep each workspace focused on its own records.

Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL, the application connects ticket handling with assets, knowledge articles and approvals. Its source includes authentication, workspace membership, private attachments and scoped API access. The device mockups show the seeded demonstration workspace (fictional users and requests), not a customer account.

A request becomes an assigned ticket with a visible status and activity trail. Agents can reply to customers, keep internal context private and link operational work to tasks. Dashboards bring outstanding requests into view so teams can decide what needs attention next.

Tenant-scoped queries and role checks support separate workspaces. Ticket transitions, attachment access and approval actions follow server-side rules. The interface brings these rules into the daily workflow through status labels, assignment controls and a consistent navigation structure.

Developed application; not deployed to a public live URL. The implemented scope covers support operations, team tasks and workspace administration. Advanced automation editors, billing checkout and live collaboration are outside the documented completed scope; integrations require their own configuration.

Ticket assignment and status transitions
Public replies and private internal notes
Project tasks, checklists and time tracking
Customer portal and knowledge articles
SLA targets, assets, departments and locations
Workspace roles, API keys and session management

The interface brings these rules into the daily workflow through status labels, assignment controls and a consistent navigation structure.

Advanced automation editors, billing checkout and live collaboration are outside the documented completed scope; integrations require their own configuration.

projects.title: Invitara
projects.overview:
Invitara is an invitation platform for weddings, engagements, birthdays, baby showers and other celebrations. Customers choose a design, personalise content and share a published guest link. The product combines animated storytelling with an editor, RSVP collection and an account dashboard.

The application uses Node.js, Express, SQLite and locally bundled animation libraries (GSAP, Motion, Anime.js and Three.js). The current collection contains independently designed invitations across many occasions, each built on a shared editor and content contract. Couple names and event details in the mockups are template placeholders, not commissioned client events.

A visitor previews a theme and creates a personalised draft before purchase. Verified checkout unlocks the purchased experience. The owner can publish a guest link, collect replies and review responses, with editing access governed by the selected event date and timezone.

The server checks purchase status and expiry for save and publish actions. Stripe redirects alone do not unlock a purchase: the application verifies signed webhook events. Password hashing, account sessions and private owner access protect the editing and RSVP workflows.

Developed application; not deployed to a public live URL. Drafts and previews work without payment credentials. Live checkout requires configured Stripe keys and webhook delivery. After the event, the editor becomes read-only and replies close while the published invitation remains available as a keepsake.

Independently designed invitation compositions
Editable content, images, theme and section order

projects.title: Mechaura International
projects.overview:
Mechaura International is an industrial supplier website organised around products, sectors and quotation enquiries. Its catalogue covers abrasive brushes, bearings, hydraulic hoses and pumps, filtration, cutting tools and elevator accessories. Product imagery and motion content help buyers understand the range before contacting the supplier.

The project uses a Vite build with generated product, sector, location and article pages, a sitemap and llms.txt workflow and optimised image assets. A companion WordPress theme packages the same design for WordPress hosting. The device mockups are captured from the production build of the website.

Buyers can enter through search, a product category, an industry or a city page, review relevant equipment and move to a quotation enquiry. The website separates product information from company and service content so technical and commercial visitors can find an appropriate next step.

Product and editorial pages are generated as static content for delivery through the website build. Images are prepared in WebP, while videos provide supporting product context. Metadata, structured data and sitemap generation keep discovery tied to the pages that the build actually publishes.

The delivered website scope is catalogue presentation and business enquiries. It is not presented as an online checkout or stock-control application. Product availability, quotation responses and fulfilment remain supplier-operated processes.

projects.title: WorkFlow Hub
projects.overview:
WorkFlow Hub is built around a common operations loop: a request arrives by email, someone reads it, assigns it, replies and follows up until it is done. It covers website, online payments, web development, store support and back-office categories. Each task has a single owner, a due date and an activity history.

The application uses Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL with session-based sign-in for administrators and employees. An AI step extracts the subject, sender, summary, category and priority from a pasted email and drafts an editable reply. The device mockups were captured from a local build running demonstration data; names, branches and tasks are fictional.

An administrator pastes an email, reviews the extracted details and the suggested reply, then creates the task and assigns an employee. The assignee is notified, updates status on the board and adds comments. The follow-up engine reminds owners before due dates and flags work that stalls.

Scheduled jobs evaluate due dates, review reminders and renewal windows against configurable thresholds. Status changes write activity logs and notifications. Role checks separate administrator screens such as employees, settings and reports from the employee workspace.

Developed internal application. Outlook mailbox integration and AI drafting depend on configured providers; drafts are always reviewed before a reply is sent from the user's own mail client.

Email-to-task intake with AI summary and reply draft
Kanban board and filterable list views
Single-owner assignment with comments and activity log
Automatic reminders, overdue flags and follow-up cadence
Domain, hosting and contract renewal tracking
Departments, branches, reports and notifications
projects.journey: An administrator pastes an email, reviews the extracted details and the suggested reply, then creates the task and assigns an employee. The assignee is notified, updates status on the board and adds comments. The follow-up engine reminds owners before due dates and flags work that stalls.
projects.engineering: Scheduled jobs evaluate due dates, review reminders and renewal windows against configurable thresholds. Status changes write activity logs and notifications. Role checks separate administrator screens such as employees, settings and reports from the employee workspace.

projects.title: DREC Property Management System
projects.overview:
The system manages the full hierarchy from landlord to internal tenant company, property and plot, unit or warehouse, subtenant and EJARI registration. Property managers track main leases and subleases, finance users follow invoices and receipts, and the dashboard summarises occupancy, contract value and upcoming expiries.

Built with Next.js 16, TypeScript, Prisma, Zustand and Recharts, with role-based access for super administrators, property managers, finance users and read-only viewers. The data model was designed from the client's lease spreadsheet. All company names, contract numbers, plot numbers and amounts in the mockups were replaced with fictional demonstration values.

A manager opens the dashboard, sees occupancy and leases approaching expiry, then drills into a property, its units and the subleases attached to them. Compliance alerts point to contracts, EJARI registrations or licences that need action, and reports export the data for review.

Each level of the hierarchy is a related record, so totals on the dashboard come from the same data the registers display. Expiry checks generate compliance alerts, and an audit log records changes. Role checks limit editing to the appropriate users.

Developed application for a property management client. Data import from the client's spreadsheets is part of the build; publication of client-identifying details requires the client's approval.

projects.title: CertGuard
projects.overview:
CertGuard centralises domains, SSL/TLS certificates, servers and DNS providers for teams that manage many websites. Instead of trusting manually entered dates, it checks domain registration data and inspects the certificate served by each site, then flags mismatches, upcoming expiries and errors.

The application uses Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL. Domain expiry comes from RDAP, certificates are inspected over a live TLS connection, and issuance follows an ACME workflow with HTTP-01 or DNS-01 validation. The mockups use the built-in demonstration data (example.com-style domains).

An administrator adds a domain; CertGuard verifies registration and certificate details and marks the record as verified or mismatched. The dashboard and notifications highlight what expires soon, and renewals can be requested, installed and verified with every step recorded.

Verification, issuance and installation are separate services behind interfaces, so providers can be swapped. Credentials and tokens are stored encrypted, deployments validate configuration before reload and roll back on failure, and every operation writes an audit entry.

Developed application. Live certificate issuance and installation require configured ACME, DNS and SSH access; without them the issuance pipeline runs in a clearly marked simulation mode.
projects.features:
RDAP domain verification and live SSL inspection
Stored-versus-discovered date comparison
ACME certificate request, renewal and rollback
SSH server registry with Nginx and Apache operations
Email, WhatsApp, Telegram and Slack alerts
Automation logs, reports and role-based access

projects.engineering: Verification, issuance and installation are separate services behind interfaces, so providers can be swapped. Credentials and tokens are stored encrypted, deployments validate configuration before reload and roll back on failure, and every operation writes an audit entry.
projects.scope: Developed application. Live certificate issuance and installation require configured ACME, DNS and SSH access; without them the issuance pipeline runs in a clearly marked simulation mode.
projects.approach: CertGuard reflects the day-to-day work of keeping dozens of domains and certificates healthy. A similar tool starts with an inventory of domains, registrars, hosting servers and who must be notified before something expires.

projects.title: Mino Suppliers
projects.overview:
Mino Suppliers combines a marketing website with a trade portal. Visitors browse sustainable tissue, towel and napkin products and apply for a wholesale account. Approved business customers sign in to order at their own pricing tier, reuse order guides, route large orders for approval and follow invoices on net terms.

Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL. Pricing tiers and customer-specific prices are resolved on the server, and orders above a company's approval threshold wait for an approver. The mockups use fictional customers and demonstration orders.

A prospective customer reads about the products, submits a wholesale enquiry and is approved by the team. Purchasers then order from the portal at their agreed prices, approvers review orders above the limit, and finance follows invoices — while admins see leads, customers, orders and revenue in one place.

Roles distinguish visitors, purchasers, approvers, company owners and staff. Prices, approval rules and payment terms come from the customer's company record, so the same catalogue shows the correct commercial terms for each account.

Developed application. Card payment, email notifications and analytics are designed as later integrations; the documented scope covers the website, portal and administration.

projects.title: JKR International
projects.overview:
JKR International supplies wheelchairs, patient-handling equipment, respiratory and diagnostic devices to hospitals, clinics and home-care customers. The platform supports both retail purchases and B2B quotation requests, with category, brand and collection browsing, product comparison, wishlists and order tracking.

The original platform was built with Django, PostgreSQL and Cloudinary; this Next.js and Prisma rebuild adds an enquiry cart, English and Arabic interface support and a custom admin panel. Product imagery in the mockups is illustrative placeholder artwork from the local demonstration build, not the client's production photography.

Clinical buyers search or browse by category and brand, compare products and either add them to the enquiry cart for a quotation or purchase directly. The team manages orders, enquiries, content and catalogue updates from the admin panel.

Catalogue, orders, enquiries and content share one data model, so admin changes appear on the storefront immediately. Payment, transactional email and media storage are integrated through configurable providers.

The original platform was built on Django; the Next.js rebuild shown here is a developed application captured locally. Payment and email providers require live credentials.

projects.title: The House of Karji
projects.overview:
The House of Karji is a custom-built fragrance store designed as an alternative to a theme-based storefront. It presents collections through an editorial home page, rich product pages with fragrance pyramids and size options, a scent quiz, store locations and a streamlined cart and checkout.

Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma, Zustand and Framer Motion. Banners, promotions, BOGO offers, advertisements, CMS pages and store locations are managed from the admin. The mockups use demonstration fragrance houses and products from the local build.

Shoppers move from campaign banners and curated collections to a product page, choose a size and add it to the cart, or use the fragrance finder when unsure. The team manages products, campaigns and orders from the admin panel.

Storefront sections read from the same catalogue and campaign tables the admin edits, so merchandising changes do not need code. Cart, wishlist and recently viewed items persist in the browser for a smooth return visit.

Developed application captured locally; the live Karji store operates on Shopify. Payment providers such as Tabby, Tamara and card gateways require live credentials.

projects.title: Carter Studio
projects.overview:
Carter Studio is a complete studio website template: services with detail pages, a filterable portfolio with case studies, transparent pricing, a blog, testimonials and a contact brief form. Every section is driven by content managed in an admin panel.

Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma, GSAP and Three.js. The admin manages projects, services, pricing plans, testimonials, skills, FAQs, blog posts, contact submissions and newsletter subscribers. The studio name and persona are fictional; the mockups were captured from the local build.

Visitors move from the hero to services and relevant case studies, compare packages on the pricing page and send a project brief. The owner updates content and reviews enquiries from the admin dashboard.

Content collections are stored in the database and rendered by shared section components, so new services or case studies appear without code changes. Sitemaps and metadata are generated from the same records.

projects.title: Rydge Studio
projects.overview:
Rydge Studio is a portfolio site for a creative studio with a home page, portfolio, project pages, services, about, blog and contact. Its visual language uses viewport-scaled typography, a strict black-and-white palette and motion such as marquees and text reveals.

Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, Prisma and SQLite, with GSAP and Lenis for motion. The design language references a commercial Webflow template and was rebuilt with original placeholder imagery and copy; the engineering work is the CMS that makes every public section editable.

Visitors scroll through the studio story, browse work and open project pages before getting in touch. The studio edits pages, sections, collections and media from the admin without touching templates.

Public templates read all content from the database rather than hard-coded copy. A signed admin session protects editing, and a seed script creates a complete demonstration site in one command.

Developed website captured locally from its seeded demonstration content.

posts.title: Architecting Unified Shopify Plus & Retail POS for UAE Luxury Brands

posts.content: Scaling omnichannel commerce in the GCC demands zero-latency inventory synchronisation and resilient POS fallbacks. In this technical deep-dive, we explore how distributed event webhooks and automated tax invoice generation ensure sub-second consistency across physical POS terminals and online checkouts.

posts.title: Building Resilient Automated Test Suites for Commercial Payments & Accounting
posts.excerpt: End-to-end regression pipelines, idempotent ledger transactions, and automated reconciliation tests for multi-currency portals.
posts.content: Financial systems fail silently when rounding errors, rate spikes, or asynchronous gateway webhooks occur. Learn the architecture of our Playwright & Node automated testing framework that guarantees transaction safety across UAE VAT reconciliation routines.

posts.title: High-Availability Infrastructure & Zero-Downtime Migration Playbook
posts.excerpt: From SSL lifecycle automation to automated failovers: maintaining 99.99% uptime for multi-tenant property management platforms.
posts.content: When managing enterprise property platforms handling thousands of tenant leases and real-time payment entries, unannounced downtime directly hits the bottom line. Here is the operational blueprint behind our DNS clustering, automated SSL renewal daemon, and Dockerized deploy workflows.
